extra.message: GET /api/exports/decision-letter/:decisionId interpolates the format query parameter into execSync(). An authenticated underwriter or administrator can supply shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands with the server's privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: The compliance-note endpoint joins request.body.noteFileName to COMPLIANCE_STAGING_DIR and writes the supplied body without checking containment. Support specialists, underwriters, and administrators can use ../ sequences to create or overwrite files outside the staging directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: The product brochure endpoint passes the caller-controlled fileName through path.join() into fs.writeFileSync(). An application administrator can use ../ sequences and arbitrary contentBase64 to overwrite files accessible to the server outside PRODUCT_ASSETS_DIR.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: PUT /api/borrowers/my permits borrowers to set letterheadFilename. The staff letterhead-preview endpoint subsequently joins that stored value to LETTERHEAD_DIR and returns the file without a containment check. A traversal value can make the preview disclose server-readable files outside the template directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: PUT /api/payment-accounts/:id/designate-primary requires authentication but never checks account ownership or staff permissions. Any borrower knowing another account's ID can promote it, demote that business's other primary accounts, and change its bankName and routingNumber.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /api/payment-accounts/ledger-sync/start has no authentication or partner verification. Anyone supplying an existing accountId receives a signed session token accepted by both ledger-sync and disbursement-sync, allowing unauthorized reconciliation-state updates.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The ledger-sync endpoint explicitly verifies JWTs with ignoreExpiration: true. A captured ten-minute sync token remains usable indefinitely to overwrite the associated account's lastLedgerSyncRunId; no consumed-token or current-run check prevents replay.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: When JWT_SECRET is unset, normal runtime authentication uses a publicly known fallback signing key. An attacker knowing an active user's ID can forge a JWT for that user, including an administrator, because authenticate() accepts signatures made with this key.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: If LEDGER_SYNC_SECRET is unset, both reconciliation callbacks trust a hardcoded signing key. An attacker can forge accountId and syncRunId claims and modify ledger or disbursement reconciliation state without possessing a legitimate partner credential.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: POST /api/admin/users assigns Welcome123! whenever password is omitted and activates the account by default. This applies to staff and administrator roles. Anyone knowing the new account's email can log in with the shared password; no forced password change is enforced.

cwe: CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password

extra.message: The live borrower-lead import creates every account with the password Welcome123!. User.isActive defaults to true, so imported borrowers can immediately be impersonated using their email and this shared password.

cwe: CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password

extra.message: Application responses serialize complete assignedTo, reviewer, and author User entities, including passwordHash and active resetToken values. Borrowers can obtain staff credentials through their own applications. The same unrestricted User serialization occurs in application lists, documents, messages, notes, decisions, and borrower-profile responses. Exposed reset tokens enable account takeover.

cwe: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

extra.message: GET /api/documents applies borrower ownership filtering only when applicationId is supplied. Omitting that optional parameter returns every borrower's document records and joined loan applications. The filter also fails open when a borrower profile is missing.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: Borrowers can upload replacements for accepted documents. The endpoint replaces the file but changes status only for requested or needs_resubmission documents, preserving accepted status and reviewedById. A borrower can therefore substitute unreviewed financial or identity evidence while retaining its approval.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Decision creation checks the underwriter role but never checks whether the application is assigned to that underwriter or belongs to their permitted queue. An underwriter can approve, reject, or counteroffer another reviewer's application. applications.ts:399 also permits taking over an existing assignment without checking its current owner.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: Every approved decision sends a new disbursement instruction without checking the application's existing status or whether payout was already initiated. Replaying or concurrently submitting approval requests creates additional decision records and repeats the banking request, with no local idempotency control.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: The approval gate examines only existing document rows and omits needs_resubmission. It never checks required DocumentTemplate entries against the application's documents. Consequently, applications with no required-document records, or documents awaiting requested replacements, can pass this gate and trigger approval and disbursement.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: GET /api/documents/templates/import fetches the arbitrary x-template-source-url header and returns the response body. An application administrator can make the server request loopback, private-network, or cloud metadata endpoints and disclose responses. This handler does not apply the neighboring preview endpoint's hostname allowlist.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery

extra.message: An unauthenticated POST to either partner-referral endpoint with Cookie: partner_session=% makes decodeURIComponent throw. Both async handlers lack rejection handling. Express 4 leaves the rejected promise unhandled, terminating the process under Node's default policy. Framework behavior is confirmed by [Express 4 source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/expressjs/express/4.18.2/lib/router/layer.js) and [Node documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v20.11.1/docs/api/cli.html#--unhandled-rejectionsmode).

cwe: CWE-248: Uncaught Exception

extra.message: The payout-draft confirmation endpoint decrypts attacker-controlled AES-CBC ciphertext without authentication and returns Invalid draft padding for padding failures, versus Malformed draft token for subsequent parsing failures. These distinguishable responses expose a padding oracle to any authenticated caller.

cwe: CWE-203: Observable Discrepancy

extra.message: When PAYOUT_DRAFT_SECRET is missing, payout drafts are encrypted using a key derived entirely from hardcoded values. Anyone obtaining a draft token can reproduce the key and decrypt or alter its bank details; the random IV does not protect against a known key.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: When COUNTEROFFER_TOKEN_SECRET is missing, counteroffer resume tokens use an AES-GCM key derived from a hardcoded secret and salt. Anyone obtaining a token can recover its loan terms or construct a modified token with a valid authentication tag.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: authenticate() verifies the shared JWT signature and user ID without checking token purpose. Password-reset JWTs generated at line 21 therefore authenticate as full sessions, even after their database resetToken value is consumed or replaced, until their signed expiry.

cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: Password reset changes passwordHash and clears reset-token fields but does not invalidate existing authentication JWTs. authenticate() checks neither password-change time nor a session version, so an attacker retaining a stolen session can continue accessing the account for the remaining 24-hour token lifetime.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: POST /api/auth/login permits unlimited password guesses. Failed comparisons do not increment an attempt counter, lock the account, or impose throttling, and index.ts installs no rate-limiting middleware. This permits unrestricted online password guessing and credential stuffing.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Email confirmation accepts unlimited guesses against a six-digit code during its fifteen-minute validity period. Incorrect submissions neither consume the code nor limit further attempts, allowing a registered user to brute-force confirmation without accessing the claimed mailbox.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Registration hashes any nonempty password without enforcing a minimum length or strength. Password reset has the same omission at line 230. Direct API callers can set one-character passwords, bypassing the frontend's length check and leaving accounts easily guessable.

cwe: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements

extra.message: Email ownership verification codes are generated with Math.random(), a noncryptographic pseudorandom generator. The security-sensitive code lacks cryptographic unpredictability and is subsequently trusted to mark the user's email as verified.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The device-trust endpoint places a valid authentication JWT in sessionId without Secure or HttpOnly, including in production. The cookie can be transmitted over HTTP and read by same-origin scripts; a stolen value is usable as a Bearer token.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: GET /api/auth/continue passes x-redirect-url, or the Referer header, directly to res.redirect(). Neither source is restricted to local paths or trusted origins, allowing authenticated requests to produce redirects to attacker-controlled websites.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Partner eligibility and referral submission treat any nonempty partner_session cookie as an authenticated partner session. No signature or server-side session lookup is performed. cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
